props.llms_description: How to pay a band or a musician through a company's accounts payable, from a Denver live-music booking company. A finance team usually wants four documents before it pays: the contract, a certificate of insurance (most venues want to be named as additional insured), a W-9 and one itemized invoice. Vendor setup is usually the slowest step, so it is worth starting the week the band is chosen. If the company pays against purchase orders, the PO number goes on the invoice. For payments made in 2026, a company files a 1099-NEC once it pays a contractor $2,000 in the year, up from $600, with the amount indexed to inflation from 2027. Booking through an agency means one vendor, one W-9, one certificate and one invoice for the whole band.

props.html: You’ve picked the band, your boss signed off, and the date is held. Then accounts payable asks for a W-9 and the band’s bank details, and the venue asks for an insurance certificate. None of it is hard, but it can take a few days.

Your finance team will want four things before it pays anyone:

  1. The contract: the date, the times, the fee, and what happens if either side cancels.
  2. A certificate of insurance: proof of liability coverage. Most venues want to be named on it as additional insured.
  3. A W-9: the band’s taxpayer ID, so your company can pay them and report it.
  4. One itemized invoice: every charge on its own line.

Ask for all four in one email when you book. Here’s what the line items on a band quote mean.

props.text: Why vendor setup takes the longest

props.html:
At most companies, a new vendor has to be set up before the first payment. That can mean a vendor form, bank details for a transfer, and sometimes a review by another department. All of it happens inside your company, on your finance team’s schedule.

So start it the week you pick the band, even if the event is months away. Here’s how long the paperwork usually takes.
If your company pays against purchase orders, send the band the PO number before they send the invoice, and ask them to put it on the invoice. An invoice without one tends to sit in a queue.

Booking five musicians directly can mean five vendor setups, five W-9s and five payments. At the end of the year, it can also mean five 1099s.

The rule on that changed this year. For payments made in 2026, a company files a 1099-NEC for a contractor once it pays them $2,000 in the year. Before 2026 it was $600, and the amount will rise with inflation starting in 2027.

Booking through an agency like Signet means one vendor, one W-9, one certificate and one invoice for the whole band.

Most bands hold a date with a signed contract and a deposit. Some will hold it on a signature alone and invoice your company after the event. Ask up front, because the answer changes who has to do what and when.

Our terms for companies are in the planner FAQ.

Ask too whether paying by card adds a processing fee. A bank transfer usually doesn’t.
